title: Falling Film Evaporator

introduction.definition: In a falling film evaporator, liquid is spread at the top of long vertical tubes and flows down the inside walls as a thin film, while steam condenses on the outside. The liquid evaporates from the film surface; vapour and concentrate leave at the bottom and are split in a separator. Residence time is short and the temperature difference small.
key_points: Thin film → high heat transfer at low ΔT
Short residence time — gentle on products
Recirculation keeps the minimum wetting rate
introduction.summary: In a falling film evaporator the liquid is distributed at the top of long vertical tubes and flows down the inside walls as a thin film, heated by steam condensing outside. Vapour and concentrate leave at the bottom and are split in a separator. Short residence time and small temperature differences suit heat-sensitive products.

temperature.title: Small temperature difference, short residence time
temperature.description: Steam condenses outside the tubes while a thin film of liquid flows down the inside walls by gravity and evaporates from its surface. Because the film is thin and there is no hydrostatic head, it works with small temperature differences and very short residence time — ideal for heat-sensitive products such as milk, juices and pharmaceuticals.

foundation: Support vessels on structure/legs designed for operating and flooded weights; allow thermal growth of calandrias and vapour lines.
alignment: Vertical calandrias plumb (falling-film distribution depends on it); slope liquor lines for drainage.
piping: Vapour lines sized for low ΔP; condensate drained by traps or level control; vents for non-condensables on each steam chest.
Vacuum system (condenser + vacuum pump/ejector) for the last effect.
commissioning: Leak/vacuum test; water trials (wetting, levels); bring steam on slowly; set levels and densities; CIP routine.

routine.task: Monitor ΔT, wetting rate and product concentration.

lubrication: Pump bearings and seals per maker.

safety: Hot surfaces and steam; vacuum vessels must be rated for full vacuum.

video_tutorials.title: Falling Film Evaporator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Falling Film Evaporator.
In a falling film evaporator, liquid is spread at the top of long vertical tubes and flows down the inside walls as a thin film, while steam condenses on the outside.
The liquid evaporates from the film surface; vapour and concentrate leave at the bottom and are split in a separator.
Residence time is short and the temperature difference small.
Typical applications include dairy (milk concentration), juices, sugar; pharmaceuticals and heat-sensitive chemicals; mechanical vapour recompression (MVR) systems.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Calandria Shell (steam chest) & Tubesheets, Top Head (feed chamber) & Bottom Head, Recirculation Pump, Recirculation Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Falling Film Evaporator works.
Feed enters the top head and the distributor wets every tube.
A thin liquid film falls down inside the tubes.
Steam condenses on the outside of the tubes.
Vapour and concentrate separate in the separator.
The recirculation pump returns liquid to the top.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Falling Film Evaporator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Falling Film Evaporator.
Monitor ΔT, wetting rate and product concentration.
CIP cleaning of tubes and distributor.
Inspect tubes; check distributor holes.
Watch for dry patches/fouling: burnt deposits, falling capacity. Common cause: poor distribution, low wetting rate.
Watch for entrainment losses: product in condensate. Common cause: separator overloaded.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
